title: The Bell Labs Formula That Keeps Smart Winners Solvent
alt_title_1: Why Betting Too Big on a Winning Edge Leads to Ruin
alt_title_2: John Kelly's 1956 Position-Sizing Rule for Investors
description_hook: In 1956, Bell Labs physicist J. L. Kelly Jr. proved mathematically why betting too much of your capital on a genuine advantage still ends in bankruptcy. Here is how Half-Kelly position sizing protects long-term compounding.

scenes.headline: How a 60% Winning Coin Still Bankrupts You
scenes.stat_label: WHY EDGE WITHOUT SIZING EQUALS RUIN
bullets: Imagine a biased coin that lands heads 60% of flips
Betting 100% of your bankroll guarantees hitting zero
scenes.narration: Even if you hold a winning coin that lands heads sixty percent of the time, betting your entire bankroll on every flip still guarantees eventual bankruptcy.
scenes.source: J. L. Kelly Jr., Bell System Technical Journal (1956)

scenes.headline: John Kelly's 1956 Bell Labs Proof
bullets: A 50% drawdown demands a 100% gain just to break even
Betting past twice the Kelly optimum shrinks wealth to zero
scenes.narration: In 1956, Bell Labs physicist John Kelly Jr. proved why in the Bell System Technical Journal: losses compound asymmetrically, because a fifty percent drop requires a one hundred percent gain just to recover.
scenes.source: J. L. Kelly Jr., 'A New Interpretation of Information Rate' (1956)

scenes.headline: Volatility Drag Wipes Out Impatient Winners
scenes.left_body: Positive edge + oversized stakes -> wiped out by 3 bad flips
scenes.right_body: Positive edge + capped stake -> survives streaks & compounds
scenes.narration: Overbetting a real advantage destroys wealth through volatility drag. One inevitable three-loss streak wipes out years of patient gains before the odds can play out.

scenes.headline: Edward Thorp's Half-Kelly Guardrail
scenes.stat_subtext: Cut theoretical max bet by 50% -> ~75% growth at half the swing
scenes.narration: Seasoned allocators like Edward Thorp apply Half-Kelly sizing: stake half the mathematical maximum on any single bet so drawdowns stay shallow and capital compounds uninterrupted.
scenes.source: Edward O. Thorp, 'The Kelly Criterion in Blackjack, Sports Betting, and the Stock Market' (1997)

scenes.headline: Stay Solvent Long Enough for Edge to Work
scenes.stat_label: NEVER LET ONE LOSS END YOUR GAME
bullets: Real-world probabilities are noisier than casino coins
Cap speculative bets so survival is never in question
scenes.narration: Cap every speculative position so no single bad outcome can ever knock you off the compounding curve.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule of thumb (advice, not a study)
